claims.text: The initial TaVCrW alloy is a disordered solid solution at 0 K.
The initial TaVCrW state may exhibit short-range order.
TaVCrW has relevant electronic density-of-states features near the Fermi level.
An MTP trained on GGA-PBE data can replace the EAM reference potential in the TaVCrW workflow.
FEP using the MTP as the reference and DFT as the target can replace thermodynamic integration.
The proposed MTP-plus-FEP method will reduce computational cost by more than 80% relative to TOR-TILD.
The proposed method will predict the melting point within 10 K of the TOR-TILD baseline.
A supercell containing at least 128 atoms is sufficient to represent SRO without material finite-size effects.
The 2000–2400 K range covers the melting transition and enough of the liquid regime to generate relevant MTP training configurations.
Finite-temperature DFT using the Mermin functional can incorporate electronic-excitation effects into the MTP training data.
Agreement with the ab initio liquid pair distribution function and local coordination environments indicates that the MTP reproduces the target phase-space distribution.
Reproducing the ab initio phase-space distribution allows FEP to converge rapidly without a continuous path of intermediate states.
The MTP provides faster energy and force evaluations than direct DFT.
Adequate phase-space overlap enables an FEP or Bennett-type estimator to recover DFT-level free-energy corrections from MTP samples.
Replacing TI with FEP avoids cumulative integration errors and TI sampling bottlenecks.
The proposed method will capture an SRO stabilization energy of approximately 2–3 meV per atom.
The resulting melting point will be consistent with experimental trends for refractory high-entropy alloys.
Omitting significant magnetic entropy may underpredict liquid stability and consequently overestimate the melting point.
GGA-PBE errors associated with V and Cr local environments at 0 K may propagate into predictions for the liquid.
The method is falsified if its free-energy result differs from TOR-TILD by more than 0.5 meV per atom at the melting point or if its cost reduction is below 80% at equal statistical uncertainty.

contradictions.description: The SRO contribution is introduced in connection with the solid initial state and a stabilization energy, but the hypothesis and boundary condition repeatedly require the MTP and supercell to capture SRO specifically in the liquid. The phase to which the claimed 2–3 meV/atom SRO stabilization applies is therefore inconsistent or insufficiently resolved.
